Pencil was my first serious attempt at building a startup: a tool for capturing and sharing the context behind your work. These notes follow its evolution from a pull-request editor to a broader context-management product, the feedback and outreach along the way, and why I ultimately chose to step back from being a founder.

What’s Pencil?

I hate explaining myself, and so do you.

I think on average every single person on this world spends too much time trying to figure out how to frame the work they do instead of actually doing it.

It’s not even for optics reasons or politics: engineers are so deep in their rabbitholes its impossible to explain to someone else who hasn’t spent the time doing it, sales people are used to their way of “doing things”, managers don’t want to reexplain every single little thing they say in every meeting.

The point is we all want to avoid unnecessary work. Work we do should speak for itself, why re-explain what you did when Pencil can do it for you?

I don’t believe in Slacking people for hours, having standup meetings or reading emails when the future doesn’t even seem bright for Google search.

Let’s be real, we need a shift in how we communicate — ask Pencil what John did yesterday, ask Pencil how to best word what you did today, ask Pencil to explain exactly how you came to that conclusion.

And agents are the future — how are they going to pick up the work you were doing? Ask Pencil for your context, ask Pencil for your progress.

And LLMs — we literally don’t use Google search anymore, people just ask ChatGPT or some other large language model. Without sending your chat to someone, how do you explain exactly what you know?

TLDR for you lazy people: Work that speaks for itself. Never explain yourself again. Context managed as you work for yourself and your team.

trypencil.dev

Never explain yourself again.

LAUNCHING ON SEPT 1, 11:59PM EST. STAY TUNED.

https://www.trypencil.dev/

Some funny promo I do to associate my identity with Pencil:

Pencil’s Journey

July 2025 - Beginnings

I met Ryan for the first time. He was building Eera which I thought was really cool. Asked if he wanted to work on something with me

I tell Ryan about my idea. I’ve been inspired by Graphite since my time at Shopify. I really liked their product and I felt like there was something I could build to make it better. It started off as a PR editor with some extra features like Cursor, which was what I wanted to show Ryan at first since context explaining was such a big deal at any company I worked at.

Ryan and I start working on v1 of Pencil. This is the PR editor idea we have initially.

We schedule some calls throughout the week with people we know. We get some feedback from people around us.

Notable people we talked to:

  • Engineering manager @ Shopify
  • Engineering manager @ Mozilla
  • Engineers @ Google, Amazon, Okta, Confluent, Cohere, Snowflake
  • Chief People Officer @ Confluent
  • Principal Engineer @ Confluent

We get some harsh feedback:

  • Your scope is too small
  • How are people going to adopt this product if it’s not integrated?
  • This product is too disruptive to the user experience
  • Windsurf, Cursor and Anthropic are already going to do this

So we iterate:

  • Native, platform first experience. Addons are preferred (Chrome Extension)
  • Bigger scope. What is the underlying problem beneath PRs? Why is context sharing such a big issue?
  • How can we future proof this for agents and LLMs?

And so we settle on the underlying issue: context sharing and explaining work over and over… Everyone has been there before.

Except we frame the problem as our failure to communicate well — everyone has different ways of understanding things, why not personalize how people understand?

August 2025 - Ramping up

Idea is forming up and we have only 1 week to build a demo for YC and apply for F25. We are going to make this deadline, and so we work 6+hours every single day after work on this. I sleep at 2AM every single day, wake up at 9AM for work, and keep building.

We enrolled in our university courses but we take the bare minimum. I’m taking 3 courses, 2 of which are not related to my major. Ryan is enrolled in only 1 course.

I stopped watching TikTok, stopped going on dates with random people, stopped fooling around.

We get some traction after posting on LinkedIn and honestly, being a little ballsy.

  • We get 15+ engineers from different teams on our waitlist
  • Confluent’s VP of developer productivity will pilot our product on a team
  • Head of Engineering @ Bree (YC21) is interested in piloting our product on a team

And so we build and pitch:

  • 70+ hours together with Ryan
    • Building for 16 hours a day, only stopping to sleep, eat and think
    • Literally this guy sleeping on the floor of my university apartment with my 2 female roommates 😭
    • Staying out until 4AM on nights to build features
  • Spending 3 hours straight pitching to engineers at Luma events
  • Demoing at Socratica
  • Spending my own money on Screen Share studio and Claude. We are serious about this

And so we promote, we have a plan.

I’m going to Switzerland and Ryan is staying in Toronto for 10 days. We aim for Aug 14 soft launch with our original clients, and an official HARD LAUNCH on Sept 1 with proper promotion and priming.

Soft launch, the good and bad

  • We get ghosted by Bree and Confluent
  • We finally have a product out in the public, but with 0 zero users now

We’re back to square one, and we are not going to be in the same country.

And so our sales in Switzerland 🇨🇭 and NYC 🇺🇸 start:

WINS:

  • 120k+ views on Reddit, 100+ leads, I converted a few to 1:1s 👀
  • 2 Linkedin campaigns launched, ~10% response rate, converted a few connections to 1:1s!
  • Over 20k+ impressions on LinkedIn for Pencil! Finally hit 1k on LinkedIn!
  • 200+ cold emails sent
  • VC cold messaged us on LinkedIn
  • Z Fellows application submitted

LOSSES:

  • 0% response rate on email
  • <100 views on X/Twitter over 1 week
  • BLOCKED by 2 directors and a VP that I cold messaged on LinkedIn
  • My dad told me to stop taking calls at 1AM in Switzerland b/c I don't need to spend this much time on Pencil 🫠

It’s our first week, we’re trying different approaches and seeing what works. It sucks being told no so many times, it really does hurt. But we have no choice, keep going or die, we can’t give up.

What I chose next

Ultimately, I decided that being a founder right now is not for me. I wanted to see firsthand what types of products were being built on the frontier.
